page: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v7 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine hosted via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 architecture alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not present, as the server contains zero GPUs.

Storage configuration includes a bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD for fast ephemeral operations, alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for external disk volumes. Network connectivity provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network routing or address attachment for external traffic.

The 8:1 memory density paired with dedicated arm64 cores offers high memory capacity per thread alongside the architectural efficiency of ARM processors. The included NVMe SSD supplies high-throughput, low-latency scratch storage. A notable constraint is that applications must support or be recompiled for arm64 execution rather than legacy x86 architectures.

This server is configured for memory-demanding tasks that benefit from dedicated ARM performance, including in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database servers with local tempdb requirements, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
